paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
core_problem: Standard RAG methods indiscriminately retrieve a fixed number of passages regardless of need, which can hinder LLM versatility, introduce unhelpful context, or lower attribution accuracy.
methodology_summary: Self-RAG trains a single language model to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand and evaluate its own output using special reflection tokens (critique tokens) that score passage relevance, factual support, and overall response quality during segment-level generation.
empirical_results: Outperforms widely adopted RAG approaches and non-retrieval baselines across six tasks, achieving higher factual and citation accuracy in long-form generation and reasoning without compromising versatility.
explicit_limitations: Indiscriminate retrieval in baseline methods can hinder model versatility; reliance on proprietary LLMs to generate initial feedback data during training.
